headers.//: no-cache means 'ask every time', NOT 'never store' — the browser keeps the file and a 304 costs a round trip with no body. Worth it: these filenames aren't content-hashed, so a stored copy would let a returning visitor run new app.js against hour-old engine modules after a deploy, and a font built from a half-updated pipeline is wrong in ways nobody would report as a bug. Worker scripts cache especially stubbornly, which is exactly how a working Width slider looked broken.
Same reasoning: app.js and the page that loads it must never lag behind the engine.
